name: Shanmugasundaram Selvam
profile: Long-time non-executive, non-independent director of Sun TV Network (on the board from 10 Aug 2009) and a major shareholder (67.7 lakh shares). Died suddenly on 10 October 2024, per Sun TV's FY2024-25 annual report.
notes: Deceased 10 Oct 2024. Source: Sun TV Network Annual Report 2024-25 (NSE), https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/SUNTV1_28082025163743_Annual_Report_2024-25.pdf

name: Tu Jian
profile: Listed once on the Hurun China Rich List (2008) at about US$150m, with wealth attributed to 'Huaxinliuhe' (investments). Searches in English and Chinese (涂建 华信六合) found no profile, company page or news coverage confirming who he is or what he does now.
notes: Could not identify. 'Huaxinliuhe' may be a transliteration of a company name (e.g. 华信/华新 六合). Not the same person as Loncin's Tu Jianhua (涂建华). A Chinese company registry check would be needed. Low priority.

name: Matthew J. Missad
current_role: Executive Chairman, UFP Industries (Grand Rapids, MI); agreed to stay through 2026
profile: Career-long UFP Industries executive (wood/composite building, packaging and industrial products). He was EVP and general counsel from 1996, CEO from July 2011 to Dec 2024 and chairman from 2023. He became executive chairman when Will Schwartz took over as CEO at the start of fiscal 2025.
interesting_fact: Became UFP's fifth CEO in its history (July 2011) after more than 25 years at the company, much of it as its top lawyer.
deep_cut_fact: Started at UFP in 1978 as a high-school student working part-time on the maintenance crew. He paid his own way through college and law school, then joined full-time in 1985 as manager of legal compliance.
notes: Press contact (Lynn Afendoulis, Director of Corporate Communications) comes from a Feb 2023 release; check a recent UFP release to confirm it is current.

name: Scott H. Baxter
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Kontoor Brands (Wrangler, Lee, Helly Hansen); director at Lowe's
profile: Has led Kontoor Brands since August 2018, when it was spun out of VF Corp as the home of Wrangler and Lee. He has been chairman since 2021. Before VF (2007-2018, including group president roles over The North Face and Vans) he spent about 20 years at Nestle, PepsiCo and Home Depot, where he was SVP running the services division.
interesting_fact: Spent the first half of his career in suits at consumer and retail companies. He now wears denim to work and says he often gives away Wrangler and Lee clothes when someone compliments them: 'It shocks people, but 99% of the time, they take it.'
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate, he turned down a job offer from the US Secret Service to start his career at Nestle.
notes: Kontoor is based in Greensboro, NC. The Brunswick Review interview (2023) is a good source of rapport material.

name: G. Zachary (Zack) Gund
profile: Member of the Cleveland Gund family, longtime major Kellogg shareholders. He founded the private-capital firm Coppermine Capital in 2002 and still runs it. He was a Kellogg/Kellanova director from Dec 2014 and later lead independent director of the WK Kellogg Co spin-off. Both board seats likely ended when Ferrero bought WK Kellogg (2025) and Mars bought Kellanova.
interesting_fact: The Gund family and the Kellogg Foundation Trust agreed to vote 21.7% of WK Kellogg's stock in favour of Ferrero's US$3.1bn takeover of the cereal maker.
deep_cut_fact: Coppermine's portfolio includes B2U, which builds grid storage from second-life EV batteries, and Little Leaf Farms, a controlled-environment lettuce grower. These are useful hooks for an energy-focused podcast.
notes: His firm's website publishes his direct work email. The Kellogg board status after the 2025 acquisitions is not confirmed from a primary source. University of Vermont BA and Kellogg (Northwestern) MBA, per third-party databases.

name: Rahul Sharma
current_role: Co-founder, Micromax Informatics; drives its AI/semiconductor pivot (MiPhi Semiconductors JV with Taiwan's Phison) and Bhagwati Products
profile: Co-founded Micromax in 2000 with Vikas Jain, Sumit Arora and Rajesh Agarwal. It began as an IT/telecom hardware firm and became one of India's top phone brands after 2008. He founded electric-motorcycle maker Revolt Intellicorp (2019), which RattanIndia fully acquired in 2023. He now focuses on electronics components, AI storage chips (MiPhi) and a Rs 250 crore deeptech family office.
interesting_fact: Micromax's MiPhi joint venture with Taiwan's Phison designs and makes AI-enabled storage chips in India. In 2026 the family set up a Rs 250 crore family office to back deeptech startups.
deep_cut_fact: Micromax's first big hit came from a trip to a village with no grid power, where a phone booth ran on a truck battery that its owner cycled to the next village each night to charge. Sharma came back and built the X1i, a phone with a 30-day battery.
notes: Many Indians share this name; this record is the Micromax co-founder. I found no published press or IR email (the only email on MiPhi's site is customer care). The truck-battery story appears in many outlets (CNN Money 2016, Business Standard 2010, YourStory), though accounts disagree on whether the village was in West Bengal or Bihar. It fits an energy angle well.
